Code splitting puts what the first paint does not need behind a dynamic import, and then the browser fetches it when the code asks. Which part of a page that is does not follow from the build output; the source decides it.
2 packages are imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

It is imported per module as well, through 2 other specifiers.

Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

15 components of @nextcloud/vue are delivered although no file in src names them, no other dependency names them and no component named by either imports them: 12,658 B, 0.1 % of the static path of portaliq-shared-nc-vue.js, next to 8 components the source names, 34 that other dependencies name and 9 those pull in.
NcRelatedResourcesPanel 6,857 B, NcFormBoxItem 1,790 B, NcEmojiPicker 1,730 B, NcSelectTags 1,174 B, NcProgressBar 315 B, NcActionButtonGroup 213 B, and 9 more.

These arrive through the root import, and @conduction/nextcloud-vue on the same page imports the root as well: as long as one module imports the barrel, the whole component set is reachable, so the bundler must keep it. Per-component imports in the app drop nothing while that package does; the specifier to change is in @conduction/nextcloud-vue.
